groupingRule: A note whose value contains ">" → group 20 (lint's note patterns stop at the first ">" and read no note).
A second note of a key the file already declared → ungrouped (lint reads the first only).
A note lint rejects or ignores — a value it cannot parse, a keyline word other than mark, grows in an outline file, gap at or over 1.5, an anchor naming its own file → ungrouped.
Any other note goes to its key's group: keyline 2 · box 3 · optical 4 · glyph 5 · grows 6 · anchor 7 · gap 8 · tags 9.
Groups 10–19 hold no notes: they are escapes that leave no mark in a file, and list drawings, measured as each panel says.

k.x: <!-- Three bars, bare: Three upright lines - low, tall, middle - and nothing else. The lightest drawing of the ten and the nearest to menu and sliders-4: the same line with the same round ends. The order is deliberate: bars that only rise read as signal strength, equal bars read as menu on its side. Bars stand on whole-number centres a quarter of the canvas apart (6 · 5 · 4; at 24 these are sliders-4's three columns, 6 / 12 / 18), so all three bars render alike and the filled bars are whole pixels at 20 and 16. Bar heights 9/18/13 · 7/14/10 · 6/12/9. Ink box 13.5x18 · 11.5x14 · 9.25x12, declared a mark. Smallest gap is the air between neighbouring bars: 4.5 · 3.5 · 2.75, filled 3.5 · 3 · 2 (floor 1.5). Filled: the repeated-elements case (C17), following menu-filled exactly - weight 2.5 · 2 · 2, ends pulled in 0.5 · 0.25 · 0.375 so the heights hold, bars thicken in place, so the filled drawing is 0.5 · 0.25 · 0.375 wider on each side (14.5 · 12 · 10 wide), declared with a grows note as menu-filled is. sliders-4-filled thickens its tracks in place too; its crossbars are what hold its box. At 16 a 1.25 line on a whole-number centre renders as two grey columns, the same as the upright of plus. Extends: stacked = each bar broken by a 1.5 gap; trend = the bars shortened under a rising line; horizontal is the weak one - three bare level lines of different lengths read as align-left or filter-2, so that variant would have to borrow C's floor line -->

Keeps the pair everyone reads as translate, and the curve is what makes the 文 a character rather than an x under a lid; at 16 it is as legible as A and no worse (recommended). The 文 is dot, bar and 乂: the dot stands on the bar (one path), the bar is 11.5 · 8 · 6.5 wide, the dot shows 2 · 1.75 · 1.75 above it; the 撇 and 捺 cross at 45° and start 1.5 below the bar instead of hanging from it (simplified: hung from the bar, the triangle between bar and crossing measures under 1.5 unless the legs start 3.3 or more from the middle, which makes the 文 7.9 wide at 16 and leaves no room for the A); upper arms 2 · 1.5 · 1, lower arms 4 · 2.75 · 1.75 on each axis (filled 1.75 · 1.25 · 0.75 and 3.25 · 2.25 · 2, the 捺 1.25 at 16 to clear the A). Filled: line-heavy, 2.5 · 2 · 2; the A keeps its leg angle, its feet pull in by half the added weight so the box holds exactly, and its apex, which no edge of the box rests on, sits 0.37 · 0.17 · 0.27 lower; the crossbar drops to the highest line that keeps the counter at 1.5 (filled counter 1.57 · 1.66 · 1.52, crossbar-to-foot 1.25 · 1 · 1).
